findings.title: V2 canManage() grants group management to holders of a VIEW permission on all groups
findings.body:
`GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` (lines 65-71) returns `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`. The no-argument `requireManage()` is what `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` calls (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/GroupsResource.java:181). A caller whose only grant is `view` on the all-groups resource therefore passes that check. The same method then accepts an `id` for an existing subgroup and calls `realm.moveGroup(child, null)` (GroupsResource.java:192-198), so the caller can also move existing groups to the top level.

Before this PR the check was role-only: `GroupPermissions.canManage()` returned `root.users().canManageDefault()`, which is `hasOneAdminRole(MANAGE_USERS)` (see the removed lines in the diff of GroupPermissions.java and UserPermissions.java). The VIEW grant is new. The Javadoc at services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:72-77 says 'For V2 only: Also if it has permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups', so the author documented it as intended. A read-only grant should not authorize writes, though.

Fix: in `canManage()`, check only `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE`, and update the Javadoc to match. Check that the change does not break the all-groups MANAGE path that `testManageAllGroups` exercises.
findings.originReason: GroupPermissionsV2 is a new file in this diff, and MgmtPermissionsV2.groups() now returns it. In the base, V2 used the V1 role-only canManage().

verification.reason: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so an all-groups VIEW grant passes requireManage() in addTopLevelGroup. That lets the caller create top-level groups and move existing subgroups to the top level. Before this change, canManage() checked only the MANAGE_USERS role.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() collects the authz resource UUID, not the group id
findings.body:
In the V2 override, the loop over `findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` adds `groupResource.getId()` (line 123). The V1 version adds the group id parsed from the resource name (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissions.java:313-315). `ClientPermissionsV2.java:138-141` uses `resource.getName()`.

For a V2 group resource the name is the group id: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` calls `resourceStore.create(server, name, owner)` with `name = resolveGroup(...) = group.getId()` (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:118-121, 181-186). The 3-arg `create` passes a null id (server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/store/ResourceStore.java:45-47), and JPAResourceStore generates a random UUID for it (model/jpa/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/jpa/store/JPAResourceStore.java:62-68). The set therefore holds UUIDs that match no group.

The set is consumed in two places. `JpaUserProvider.groupsWithPermissionsSubquery` matches `groupId in (...)` against membership rows (model/jpa/.../JpaUserProvider.java:1059-1070). `getUsersCount(realm, Set)` returns 0 for an empty set (JpaUserProvider.java:599-602).

Visible effect: for a V2 user whose only access is group-membership view, the user list (`UsersResource.searchForUser`, UsersResource.java:448-453) is post-filtered by `canView` (UsersResource.java:460) and shows the user. The count path (`UsersResource.java:430`, `getUsersCount(realm, getGroupIdsWithViewPermission())`) returns 0. With an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grant the set becomes non-empty with a UUID that matches nothing, so the list is restricted to zero users.

Also check that the type is set. Nothing in the create path calls `setType` for V2 group resources (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:118-128), and `ResourceEntity.type` has no default (model/jpa/.../ResourceEntity.java:91). Without a type, `findByType("Groups")` returns only the type-level resource. V1 sets `setType("Group")` explicitly (GroupPermissions.java:117).

Fix: return `groupResource.getName()`, and make per-group V2 resources carry the Groups type so the loop sees them. Note that `testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers` passes only because the list is post-filtered; it does not check the count.

The loop adds groupResource.getId(), which is that UUID, unlike V1 and ClientPermissionsV2, which use the name. Per-group V2 resources also get no type, so findByType("Groups") returns only the type-level "Groups" resource. The result is that the set is empty or holds a UUID that matches no group.

findings.title: Javadoc of requireManageMembers names the wrong check
findings.body: The Javadoc on `requireManageMembers` says 'Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns false', but the method is declared at line 135 and `GroupPermissions.requireManageMembers` calls `canManageMembers` (GroupPermissions.java:376-380). Change the link to `#canManageMembers(GroupModel)`.

findings.title: Dropping the canViewGlobal shortcut may hide groups that have their own permission resource
findings.body:
Before this PR, `GroupsResource` and `GroupResource.getSubGroups` (GroupResource.java:179) checked `canView()` once and returned all groups when it was true. They now call `canView(group)` for every group. In V2, `canView(group)` checks only the group's own resource when one exists (GroupPermissionsV2.java:141-150; `hasPermission(group.getId(), ...)` never falls back to the all-groups resource in that case).

The typed-resource branch in `DefaultPolicyEvaluator` runs only when `resource.getType() != null` (server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/policy/evaluation/DefaultPolicyEvaluator.java:73-80). Per-group V2 resources have no type (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:118-128). The all-groups VIEW grant could therefore be missed for such groups. It may still be found through the scope-based lookup at DefaultPolicyEvaluator.java:84-88, which I did not trace.

The V2 user check filters permissions by resource id (UserPermissionsV2.java:122-123). The V2 group check does not. Please confirm that a group which has its own permission resource still appears in the list when the caller holds all-groups VIEW.
findings.originReason: Both the V2 group evaluator and the removal of the canViewGlobal shortcut are in this diff.

verification.reason: If a group has its own resource, hasPermission evaluates only that resource. DefaultPolicyEvaluator then finds no all-groups policy: the per-group resource has no type, and findByScopes(null) matches only permissions without resources, but the all-groups permission is attached to the "Groups" resource. So all-groups VIEW does not show such groups, and the canViewGlobal shortcut that would have covered them was removed.

findings.title: Per-group canView evaluation in the group list
findings.body: `stream.filter(groupsEvaluator::canView)` (GroupsResource.java:113) and the same change in `GroupResource.getSubGroups` (GroupResource.java:179) run a permission evaluation for every group when the caller relies on a V2 all-groups grant. Previously one `canView()` evaluation covered all rows. Consider evaluating the global grant once and filtering per group only when it is false.
findings.originReason: This diff removed the canViewGlobal shortcut.

verification.reason: Without the canViewGlobal shortcut, a V2 caller without user roles triggers findByName, findByResource and a policy evaluation for every listed group. Before, one global check could cover the whole list.

findings.title: Group-view user test checks only the list, not the count
findings.body: `testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers` asserts only the result of `users().search(...)`. The count endpoint takes the group-id path that the V2 bug above breaks (UsersResource.java:427-431), so the count can be 0 while this list returns Alice. Add a `users().count()` assertion for the same scenario so the test covers both paths.
findings.originReason: This test file is new in this diff.

verification.reason: The test asserts only users().search(). The count path goes through getGroupIdsWithViewPermission (UsersResource.java:430), which is broken in V2, and no test covers it.

contracts.action: POST /groups (top-level create) and move of an existing group to top level via rep.id, now gated by requireManage() on V2
contracts.before_after: Before: V2 canManage() was role-only (GroupPermissions.canManage -> root.users().canManageDefault() -> hasOneAdminRole(MANAGE_USERS), per the diff). After: MANAGE_USERS, or any VIEW or MANAGE grant on the all-groups resource (GroupPermissionsV2.java:65-71).
contracts.visible_effect: A caller with only an all-groups view grant can create a top-level group and move existing subgroups to top level (GroupsResource.java:192-198).
contracts.failure_mode: Privilege escalation: a read-only grant authorizes writes. Reported as a blocker.

contracts.action: Group-based user list and count (new GROUPS session attribute and getUsersCount with group ids) for V2 callers without canView
contracts.equivalent_path: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissions.java:313-315 (V1 name-based group id extraction) and services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:138-141 (V2 uses getName())
contracts.before_after: V1 returns group ids parsed from resource names. V2 (this PR) returns the authz resource UUID via getId() (GroupPermissionsV2.java:123). Also, V2 finds per-group resources by type, which they do not carry (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:118-128).
contracts.visible_effect: The user count can be 0 while the list shows users (UsersResource.java:430 vs the post-filter at UsersResource.java:460). With an all-groups members grant the restriction matches no group, so the list is empty.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent wrong result. No data exposure: the list is still post-filtered by canView.

contracts.action: Group list filter per group via groupsEvaluator::canView (replaces canViewGlobal shortcut)
contracts.equivalent_path: Pre-PR shortcut: canViewGlobal computed once, then canViewGlobal || canView(g) per group (removed in this diff)
contracts.before_after: Before: one global check, then per-group only if false. After: per-group canView(g) for every group. In V2, canView(g) with an existing per-group resource evaluates that resource only (GroupPermissionsV2.java:141-150).
contracts.visible_effect: Possibly groups with their own permission resource are hidden from a caller who holds all-groups VIEW. Also one policy evaluation per group.
contracts.failure_mode: Possibly a silent under-disclosure in the group list; cost scales with the group count.
contracts.open_question: Does a group that has its own V2 permission resource (type unset) still receive the all-groups VIEW grant through the findByScopes lookup at DefaultPolicyEvaluator.java:84-88? If not, groups disappear from the list.

contracts.action: AdminPermissions group-removed listener: calls management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false) on GroupRemovedEvent
contracts.equivalent_path: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/MgmtPermissions.java:234-239 (base GroupPermissions, which handled this before V2 overrides were added)
contracts.before_after: Before: MgmtPermissionsV2 did not override groups(), so the V1 deletePermissions path ran under V2. After: MgmtPermissionsV2.groups() returns GroupPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled throws (GroupPermissionsV2.java:173-175). The listener is registered only when the V1 flag is on (AdminPermissions.java:74).
contracts.visible_effect: With both flags on, group deletion should fail.
contracts.failure_mode: Visible error on group delete. Event listener exceptions are not caught (DefaultKeycloakSessionFactory.java:86-90).
contracts.open_question: Which code path fires GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent during a group delete request, and does its caller propagate the listener exception?

contracts.action: GET and PUT /groups/{id}/management/permissions under V2 (isPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, setPermissionsEnabled)
contracts.before_after: Before: V2 inherited the working V1 GroupPermissions. After: GroupPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException for these methods (GroupPermissionsV2.java:168-210).
contracts.visible_effect: Both endpoints return 500 when both flags are on.
contracts.failure_mode: Visible server error on the endpoints.

contracts.before_after: Before: the filter ran twice (once in searchForUser, once in toRepresentation). After: once, in toRepresentation. The same holds for BruteForceUsersResource.java:160.
contracts.visible_effect: None. The removal is a no-op.

contracts.action: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource for resourceType Groups: new resolveGroup path
contracts.before_after: Before: the Groups type gave name null and threw 'Could not map resource' (114-116). After: resolveGroup resolves the id only, with no name fallback.
contracts.visible_effect: Permissions can be created for groups addressed by id. Unknown ids still throw the same exception.

contracts.action: UserPermissionsV2.canMapRoles and canManageGroupMembership rewritten (ADMIN role dropped; scope and group-chain checks inlined)
contracts.equivalent_path: Pre-PR: canManage(user) plus hasPermission(MAP_ROLES / MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP). canManage(user) already included canManageByGroup(user).
contracts.before_after: Equivalent for the group chain and the MANAGE scope. The only change is that the ADMIN role is no longer checked directly (UserPermissionsV2.java:48,57), so the check relies on the composite role being expanded in the token.
contracts.open_question: Does a token that carries only the realm-admin composite (not manage-users) still satisfy MANAGE_USERS after ADMIN was removed from these checks?

contracts.action: GroupPermissions.canViewMembers now includes MANAGE_MEMBERS, and getAccess reports viewMembers from it
contracts.equivalent_path: Pre-PR requireViewMembers used getGroupsWithViewPermission(group), which already checked VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS (removed in the diff)
contracts.before_after: Before: canViewMembers checked VIEW_MEMBERS only, while requireViewMembers allowed MANAGE_MEMBERS. After: both agree on VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS, as the Javadoc states.
contracts.visible_effect: The access flag viewMembers is now true for MANAGE_MEMBERS holders, matching the endpoint behaviour.

contracts.equivalent_path: Previous code: explicit response.close() after reading the location
contracts.before_after: Before: close only on success. After: close on every exit, including failed assertions.

summary: Reviewed all 19 files in this part by reading the diff, the head versions of the changed V1/V2 permission classes, and the call sites and stores they depend on. I did not build or run anything. ModelToRepresentation.java, RolePermissions.java, UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java and parts of GroupResource/GroupsResource/UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource were checked by grep and targeted reads rather than end to end. The most serious problem is the V2 `canManage()` grant: a VIEW permission on all groups authorizes top-level group creation and moving existing groups (blocker). The V2 group-id collection returns authz resource UUIDs instead of group ids, so the group-view user count is wrong (fix). Two further fixes cover V2 methods that throw under the combined admin FGAP flags, and a question on whether the dropped canViewGlobal shortcut hides groups. Imports and the compile-level changes I checked look correct. I did not verify the group-removal event path or the composite-role expansion; those are recorded as open contracts.

entries.title: With both admin FGAP flags on, V2 group-permission methods throw; group deletion and the management-permissions endpoints break
entries.reason: V1 and V2 cannot both be enabled. ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ and ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 share the unversioned key admin-fine-grained-authz. Profile.configure throws if both versions are enabled explicitly, and it marks only one version of each feature as enabled. So the listener and the GroupResource endpoints guarded by the V1 flag can never reach MgmtPermissionsV2.
